content: 1. Brigatinib's efficacy may be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to increased metabolism. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 2. Rifampin decreases brivaracetam levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification is required, with a potential dose increase of up to 100%. Monitor closely. 3. Rifampin reduces bromocriptine levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Rifampin decreases budesonide levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 5. Rifampin reduces buprenorphine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For subdermal implants, monitor for withdrawal symptoms, and consider implant removal if necessary. Adjust buprenorphine dosage as clinically appropriate. 6. Rifampin decreases buprenorphine transdermal levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, increase the transdermal dosage and monitor for opioid withdrawal. Reduce dosage if the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued. 7. Rifampin reduces buprenorphine long-acting injection levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels and consider transitioning to a formulation that allows dose adjustments if necessary. 8. Rifampin decreases bupropion levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Rifampin reduces buspirone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Rifampin decreases butabarbital and butalbital levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Rifampin reduces cabazitaxel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 12. Rifampin increases cabotegravir metabolism, reducing systemic exposure and potentially compromising virologic response. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Rifampin decreases cabozantinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or increase cabozantinib dosage as clinically appropriate. 14. Rifampin reduces caffeine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 15. Rifampin decreases calcifediol levels by enhancing microsomal hydroxylation. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 16. Rifampin reduces calcitriol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Calcium carbonate reduces rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin at least one hour before antacids. Monitor closely. 18. Rifampin decreases canagliflozin levels by inducing metabolism. Use caution and consider alternative antihyperglycemic agents for patients with renal impairment. 19. Rifampin reduces cannabidiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 20. Rifampin decreases capivasertib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Rifampin reduces capmatinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Rifampin decreases carbamazepine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Rifampin reduces cariprazine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Rifampin decreases carvedilol levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Rifampin reduces caspofungin levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ceftobiprole increases rifampin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Rifampin decreases celecoxib levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 28. Rifampin reduces cenobamate levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Adjust CYP2B6 substrate doses as needed. 29. Rifampin decreases ceritinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Rifampin reduces cevimeline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Rifampin decreases chloramphenicol levels by increasing metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 32. Rifampin reduces chlordiazepoxide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Rifampin decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Rifampin increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing elimination. Avoid bile salt efflux pump inhibitors and monitor liver function if co-administration is necessary. 35. Rifampin reduces cilostazol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Rifampin decreases cimetidine levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 37. Rifampin reduces cinacalcet levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Rifampin decreases citalopram levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Rifampin reduces clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Clofazimine reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 41. Rifampin decreases clomipramine levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Rifampin reduces clonazepam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Rifampin increases clopidogrel metabolism to its active metabolite. Monitor for enhanced antiplatelet effects. 44. Rifampin decreases clorazepate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clotrimazole increases rifampin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cotrimoxazole increases rifampin concentrations, potentially raising toxicity risk. Monitor for adverse reactions during co-administration. 47. Rifampin reduces clozapine levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Rifampin decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 49. Rifampin reduces cobimetinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Rifampin decreases colchicine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 51. Rifampin reduces conivaptan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Rifampin decreases conjugated estrogens levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 53. Rifampin reduces copanlisib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 54. Rifampin decreases cortisone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 55. Rifampin reduces crizotinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Rifampin decreases cyclophosphamide levels by inducing CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Rifampin reduces cyclosporine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
